questions.question_text: Find the global maximum of $f(x) = x^{2} - 4x + 1$ on $0 \le x \le 5$.

options.why: Took the left endpoint value $f(0)$ without comparing it with the right endpoint.
Gave the stationary value $f(2)$, which is the global minimum, not the maximum.

questions.solution_text:
$f'(x) = 2x - 4$
Set $f'(x) = 0$:
$x = 2$, which is inside the domain.
$f(2) = 4 - 8 + 1 = -3$
Endpoints:
$f(0) = 1$
$f(5) = 25 - 20 + 1 = 6$
The global maximum is $6$, at the endpoint $x = 5$.

questions.question_text: Find the global minimum of $f(x) = x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 9x + 2$ on $-2 \le x \le 5$.

options.why: Compared only the two endpoints and missed the stationary point inside the domain.
Gave the local maximum value $f(-1)$ instead of the smallest value.
Evaluated $f(0)$, which is neither a stationary point nor an endpoint.

questions.question_text: Find the global maximum of $f(x) = x^{3} - 6x^{2} + 5$ on $5 \le x \le 8$.

options.why: Chose the smaller endpoint value, which is the global minimum rather than the maximum.
Used the stationary point at $x = 4$, which lies outside the domain.
Used the stationary point at $x = 0$, which also lies outside the domain.

questions.solution_text:
$f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 12x$
Set $f'(x) = 0$:
$3x(x - 4) = 0$
$x = 0$ or $x = 4$, neither inside $5 \le x \le 8$.
Endpoints:
$f(5) = 125 - 150 + 5 = -20$
$f(8) = 512 - 384 + 5 = 133$
The global maximum is $133$, at $x = 8$.

questions.question_text: Find the global minimum of $f(x) = x + \dfrac{25}{x}$ on $1 \le x \le 10$.

options.why: Compared only the two endpoints and took the smaller of those.
Gave the largest of the candidate values, which is the global maximum, not the minimum.

questions.solution_text:
$f'(x) = 1 - \dfrac{25}{x^{2}}$
Set $f'(x) = 0$:
$x^{2} = 25$
$x = 5$, taking the value in the domain.
$f(5) = 5 + 5 = 10$
Endpoints:
$f(1) = 1 + 25 = 26$
$f(10) = 10 + 2.5 = 12.5$
The global minimum is $10$, at $x = 5$.

The graph rises to a turning point near $x = 1$, falls to another near $x = 3$, then rises steeply to the right endpoint.
The highest point on the whole domain is the right endpoint at $x = 5$.
Reading its height from the vertical scale gives $y = 40$.
The global maximum value is $40$.

questions.question_text: A function $f$ is continuous on $2 \le x \le 9$. Its only stationary point is at $x = 5$, where $f(5) = 20$. Also $f(2) = 14$ and $f(9) = 23$. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The global maximum is $23$, at the endpoint $x = 9$.
The global maximum is $20$, at the stationary point $x = 5$.
options.why: Assumed the global maximum must be at a stationary point, but the endpoint value $23$ is larger.

options.text: The global minimum is $20$, at the stationary point $x = 5$.
options.why: Took the stationary value as the minimum without comparing it with $f(2) = 14$.

options.text: The global maximum is $23$ and the global minimum is $20$.
options.why: Found the correct maximum but overlooked the smaller endpoint value $f(2) = 14$.

questions.solution_text:
The candidates are $x = 5$, $x = 2$ and $x = 9$.
The values are $f(5) = 20$, $f(2) = 14$ and $f(9) = 23$.
The largest is $23$ and the smallest is $14$.
The global maximum is $23$, at the endpoint $x = 9$.

questions.question_text: The function $f(x) = x^{3} + kx$ has a global minimum of $-54$ on $0 \le x \le 4$, occurring at a stationary point. Find $k$.

options.why: Solved $27 + k = -54$ instead of $27 + 3k = -54$, forgetting to multiply $k$ by $x = 3$.
Solved $27 - 3k = -54$, dropping the sign of $k$ when substituting into $f(x)$.

questions.solution_text:
$f'(x) = 3x^{2} + k$
Let the stationary point be at $x = p$, so $3p^{2} + k = 0$ and $k = -3p^{2}$.
$f(p) = p^{3} - 3p^{3}$
$= -2p^{3}$
Set $-2p^{3} = -54$:
$p^{3} = 27$
$p = 3$, which is inside $0 \le x \le 4$.
$k = -3(3)^{2} = -27$
Checking the endpoints: $f(0) = 0$ and $f(4) = 64 - 108 = -44$, both greater than $-54$.
So $k = -27$.
